tasks.title: PromptCheckpointStore and ServerPromptStateStore share one storage config but keep independent disk budgets (up to 2x limit on disk)
tasks.discovered-by: subagent manual pass + main-agent verification
tasks.evidence-before: Both stores were handed the same ServerPromptCacheStorageConfiguration, each with the full --prompt-cache-disk-mib budget, and each indexes the shared directory but evicts only its own records (checkpoint keys are content hashes, turn keys are UUIDs, and both indexers skip what they cannot decode). A multi-prefix session could therefore occupy twice the configured cap. The review extension: with TINYTITAN_PROMPT_CHECKPOINTS=0 the checkpoint store is never constructed, so records left by an earlier enabled run are charged to nobody, and a half-budget checkpoint cache plus a full-budget turn store reached one and a half times the cap.
tasks.fix-summary: promptCachePerStoreDiskLimit gives each store half while both exist and the whole when only one does. With checkpoints off, reclaimStaleCheckpoints constructs a zero-budget checkpoint store over the same root, calls removeAll (which indexes first, per AUD2-046) and returns the bytes that refused deletion; the turn store is then configured with the budget minus those survivors, so an undeletable record stays charged instead of disappearing. With checkpoints on, the store indexes at startup, so a restart holding more than its half is evicted before the turn store fills the other half rather than at the first capture. checkpointsEnabled is now a named function rather than an inline environment read. No change to what either store writes or to any eviction threshold.
tasks.evidence-after: RED is compile-only and is disclosed as such: against the pre-fix tree the four budget tests do not build because the seam does not exist ("type 'ServerModelSession' has no member 'promptCachePerStoreDiskLimit'", exit 1, AUDIT/aud2-003-red.log) -- there is no behavioral RED, so the bound rests on the arithmetic above plus the tests over the helpers. GREEN: AUDIT/aud2-003-green.log, 4 tests, exit 0 -- the split both ways, checkpoints on unless explicitly disabled, stale records reclaimed when disabled, and an immutable (undeletable) record returning its 16 bytes so the turn store gets budget minus 16. tasks.title: expandExpertInPlace trusts layout ordering (target >= source, target+size <= slot) without validation; a violating layout silently clobbers unread source bytes
tasks.discovered-by: RANS/C-kernel subagent pass + main-agent verification
tasks.evidence-before: expandExpertInPlace (TwoBitExpand.swift:146) rewrites a compact 2-bit blob into the 4-bit slot in place, walking an [ExpertBlobTensor] map built straight from the manifest's sub-tensor offsets and sizes (Model+LayerStreamers.swift:367-377) — untrusted file data. A map whose write region reaches a lower tensor's still-unread source, whose target sits before its source, or whose sizes do not match the transform does not crash: it decodes wrong weights and publishes them as a valid expert. tasks.title: Lazy disk indexing evicts a record loaded before the first index first, and latches done when the directory listing fails
tasks.discovered-by: independent checkpoint review of c5e2e93 (reviewer Q4), re-derived against the code by the main agent
tasks.evidence-before: Two manifestations, one cause. (a) load() inserts a record it finds on disk into state.disk and touchDisk appends it to an empty diskLRU before indexing has run; indexDiskIfNeeded then skips that key (`guard state.disk[key] == nil`) and appends the older records behind it, so the just-touched record sits at the LRU front and eviction removes it before records whose directories are older. (b) diskIndexed is set true before contentsOfDirectory is attempted, and its error is folded into an empty list, so one failed listing (root removed, EACCES, EIO) disables indexing for the lifetime of the store: removeAll then unlinks nothing and contains/metadata keep answering from direct lookup and an empty index. The turn store's loadEntries does not share either shape -- it is called at startup, resets the index, and retries on the next call.
tasks.fix-summary: indexDiskIfNeeded sets diskIndexed only after contentsOfDirectory succeeds, so a failed listing retries on the next call instead of latching; and it merges state.diskLRU with the indexed records by date -- the filesystem mtime for indexed records, the write/touch time for in-process ones -- instead of appending the listing behind a record loaded before the index. No format, budget or eviction-limit change.
tasks.evidence-after: RED on the pre-fix tree: AUDIT/aud2-046-red.log, 2 tests / 4 issues / exit 1 -- aRecordLoadedBeforeIndexingKeepsItsPlaceInTheLRU failed with the backdated record surviving and the newest evicted (three assertions), aFailedListingDoesNotLatchIndexingOff failed on the surviving directory after the root was replaced by a regular file for one call. GREEN after the fix: AUDIT/aud2-046-green.log, 30 checkpoint tests, exit 0. Full serial suite on the fix: 7 bundles, 1,995 tests, exit 0 (AUDIT/aud2-046-full.log); all 18 lint gates exit 0 (AUDIT/aud2-046-lint.log). The failed-listing fixture is deterministic (ENOTDIR), not permission-based, so it does not depend on the runner's Full Disk Access.

tasks.title: The CI markdown-link step fails on the audit's own records: path:line links and code spans read as links
tasks.discovered-by: running the 'Check Markdown links' step verbatim locally while closing AUD2-031 (AUDIT/aud2-051-markdown-link-check.log)
tasks.evidence-before: ruby script extracted from ci.yml:1061-1096, run at b719a4a on a clean tree (ruby 2.6.10p210, system ruby -- the runner uses the same interpreter family): 'Checked 365 local link(s); 19 broken', exit 1 (AUDIT/aud2-051-markdown-link-check.log). Two distinct causes. (1) Seventeen links in audit_2310.md are written as `[Foo.swift:352-377](sources/.../Foo.swift:352-377)`: the URL carries a ':lines' suffix that is neither a path nor a fragment, so File.exist? is false and GitHub could not resolve it for a reader either. docs/ already uses the other form -- text 'PreadExpertStreamer+Plan.swift:95-106' with URL '...swift#L95' -- and 179 markdown links in the tree use an '#L' anchor against 167 plain paths and these 17 suffixes. Each of the 17 cited ranges was checked against its file and is in range, so this is link syntax, not a stale citation. (2) Two code spans -- 'offsets: `[UInt64](repeating: 0, count: ...)`' in audit_2310.md:695 and the same Swift text rendered into AUDIT/ledger.md:178 -- match the link regex because the step scans raw lines, so a bracketed Swift initializer followed by a paren becomes a 'link'. Exposure: audit_2310.md and the AUDIT/*.md files are tracked only on audit/2026-10-23 (git ls-tree main shows neither), and the workflow triggers are push to main and pull_request, so no CI run has executed this step over these files yet; the first PR that carries them fails it. The filing of this record raised the same count from 19 to 24 (AUDIT/aud2-051-filing-run.log, 370 links checked): five more matches came from the new section's own code spans and its ellipsis-path examples -- writing about the defect in markdown trips the defect, which is the clearest available demonstration that the scanner has no notion of code spans.
tasks.fix-summary: Two parts, each addressing one measured cause. (1) The CI step: the ruby scanner now tracks fenced blocks (``` and ~~~) and strips paired inline code spans from a line before matching, so literal Swift text is no longer read as a link.
